drops.name: St. Abraham of the High Mountain
St. Abraham the Great of Kashkar
St. Benjamin the Deacon and Martyr
St. Denise, Dativa, Leontia, Tertius, Emilianus, Boniface, Majoricus, and Servus
St. Elizabeth, mother of John the Baptist
St. Faustina and Liberata of Como
St. Gregory of Nazianzus the Elder
St. Helena, mother of Constantine I
St. Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor
St. John III of the Sedre
St. Martha, mother of Simeon Stylites the Younger
St. Metropolitan Michael I of Kiev
St. Patriarch Cyril II of Alexandria
St. Patriarch Michael II of Alexandria
St. Patriarch Peter IV of Alexandria
St. Peter the Hermit of Galatia
Sts. Sapor, Isaac, Mahanes, Abraham, and Simeon
St. Severinus of Sanseverino and Victorinus of Camerino
St. Tassilo III, Duke of Bavaria
St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
St. Æthelberht II of East Anglia
St. Wenceslaus I, Duke of Bohemia
St. Zechariah, father of John the Baptist

matches.name: St. Anthony of Padua
matches.ceNote: Long article on the Augustinian canon turned Franciscan, priest, preacher, miracle worker, d. 1231. Known as 'the Hammer of the Heretics.'

matches.name: St. Dymphna
matches.ceNote: Virgin and martyr, venerated since at least the thirteenth century

matches.name: St. Francis of Assisi
matches.ceNote: Long article on St. Francis, founder, mystic, perhaps the most beloved Catholic saint of all

matches.name: St. Michael the Archangel
matches.ceNote: Article about this angel in Scripture and tradition

matches.name: St. Fabiola
matches.ceNote: Divorced, remarried, widowed, penitent, renowned for her generosity. She died in 399 or 400

matches.name: St. John Chrysostom
matches.ceNote: Long biographical article on this bishop and Doctor of the Church

matches.name: St. Kilian
matches.ceNote: Missionary, bishop of Wuerzburg, martyred with his companions Colman and Totnan in about 689

matches.name: St. Melania the Younger
matches.ceNote: Granddaughter of St. Melania the Elder, and a friend of St. Jerome

matches.name: St. Sidonius Apollinaris
matches.ceNote: Christian author and Bishop of Clermont, b. at Lyons, 5 November, about 430; d. at Clermont, about August, 480

matches.name: Pope Evaristus
matches.ceNote: Sometimes called Aristus. Martyr, died about 107

matches.name: St. Anastasius Sinaita
matches.ceNote: Profile of the seventh-century abbot of the monastery of Mt. Sinai, vociferous opponent of the Monophysites and Monothelites, writer

matches.name: St. Arialdo
matches.ceNote: A canon of Milan, reformer, martyr, murdered by agents of the bishop of Milan in 1065

matches.name: St. Bernard of Menthon
matches.ceNote: Archdeacon of Aosta, preacher, founder of two hospices for travelers in dangerous Alpine passes (now named the Great St. Bernard and Little St. Bernard, after him), d. 1008

matches.name: St. Clement of Alexandria
matches.ceNote: Fairly lengthy article on his life and writings

matches.name: St. Corbinian
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Freising, in Bavaria, born about 680 at Chatres near Melun, France; died 8 September, 730

matches.name: St. Diodorus of Tarsus
matches.ceNote: Date of birth uncertain; d. about A.D. 392. He was of noble family, probably of Antioch. St. Basil calls him a 'nursling' of Silvanus, Bishop of Tarsus, but whether this discipleship was at Antioch or at Tarsus is not known

matches.name: St. Edmund the Martyr
matches.ceNote: Short biography of the King of East Anglia, who died in 870

matches.name: St. Epiphanius of Salamis
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on the fourth-century monk and bishop

matches.name: St. Eulogius of Córdoba
matches.ceNote: Writer, martyr, elected Archbishop of Toledo shortly before he was beheaded (11 March, 859)

matches.name: St. Eusebius of Caesarea
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on the 'Father of Church History.'

matches.name: St. Gottschalk
matches.ceNote: Wendish prince, considered a martyr, d. 1066

matches.name: St. Justus
matches.ceNote: The first bishop of Rochester, and later the fourth archbishop of Canterbury, died possibly in 627

matches.name: St. Macrina the Younger
matches.ceNote: Granddaughter of St. Macrina the Elder, and the sister of St. Gregory of Nyssa. She died in 379

matches.name: St. Mamertus
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Vienne, d. around 476

matches.name: St. Marcus Eremita
matches.ceNote: A theologian and ascetic writer of some importance in the fifth century

matches.name: St. Martin of Braga
matches.ceNote: Missionary, monastic founder, archbishop, ecclesiastical writer, d. 580

matches.name: St. Maurus
matches.ceNote: Deacon, disciple of St. Benedict. Portrayed by St. Gregory the Great as a model of monastic obedience. Died 584

matches.name: St. Miltiades
matches.ceNote: Died in 314. An African, his name is also sometimes given as Miltiadea or Melchiades

matches.name: St. Paul the Simple
matches.ceNote: Monk, disciple of St. Antony, d. around 339

matches.name: St. Peter Igneus
matches.ceNote: So-called because he successfully underwent trial by fire. Vallombrosian monk, Cardinal of Albano, d. 1089

matches.name: St. Peter of Sebaste
matches.ceNote: Brother of SS. Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa, and Macrina the Younger. Peter was bishop of Sebaste, and died in 391

matches.name: St. Pierius
matches.ceNote: Priest and probably head master of the catechetical school at Alexandria (d. after 309)

matches.name: St. Stephen Harding
matches.ceNote: English Cistercian, confessor, the third abbot of Citeaux, d. 1134

matches.name: St. Thomas Becket
matches.ceNote: Biography of this martyr, also known as St. Thomas of Canterbury, where he was archbishop and where he was murdered in 1170

matches.name: St. Vladimir the Great
matches.ceNote: Biography of the grandson of St. Olga. Grand Duke of Kiev and All Russia, first ruler of Russia to convert to Christianity, d. 1015

matches.name: Pope Gelasius I
matches.ceNote: An assessment of his pontificate. He died in 496

matches.name: St. Adeodatus II
matches.ceNote: Brief article on this Roman monk, opponent of Monothelitism, d. 676. Called Adeodatus II to distinguish him from his predecessor St. Deusdedit, who is also called Adeodatus

matches.name: St. Adrian III
matches.ceNote: Short article on this pope, a Roman, who died in 885

matches.name: St. Adrian of Canterbury
matches.ceNote: African-born Benedictine abbot, d. 710

matches.name: St. Aelia Flaccilla
matches.ceNote: Empress, wife of Theodosius the Great, died c. A.D. 385 or 386

matches.name: St. Afra
matches.ceNote: Martyred at Augsburg in the Diocletian persecution (c. 304) for refusing to participate in pagan rites

matches.name: St. Aidan of Lindisfarne
matches.ceNote: Irish monk, first bishop of Lindisfarne, d. 651

matches.name: St. Aldhelm
matches.ceNote: Abbot of Malmesbury, bishop of Sherborne, poet, d. about 709

matches.name: St. Amphilochius of Iconium
matches.ceNote: Fourth-century Cappadocian bishop

matches.name: St. Andrew the Scot
matches.ceNote: Brother of St. Bridget the Younger and archdeacon of Fiesole, d. about 877

matches.name: St. Assicus
matches.ceNote: St. Patrick's coppersmith, also a renowned bellfounder, Bishop of Elphin

matches.name: St. Atto of Pistoia
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Pistoia (1070-1155)

matches.name: St. Auxentius of Mopsuestia
matches.ceNote: Although he is identified in the Roman Martyrology, at least one scholar thinks that this bishop was an Arian

matches.name: St. Benignus
matches.ceNote: Known as 'Patrick's psalm-singer,' Irish missionary, musician, bishop, legislator, d. 467

matches.name: St. Burchard of Würzburg
matches.ceNote: First bishop of Wuerzburg, d. about 754

matches.name: St. Caesarius of Arles
matches.ceNote: Bishop, theologian, renowned as a popular preacher, wrote two monastic rules, died 543

matches.name: St. Celestine I
matches.ceNote: Excommunicated Nestorius, sent St. Patrick to Ireland, d. 432

matches.name: St. Chromatius
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Aquileia, anti-Arian theologian, tried to reconcile Rufinus and Jerome, d. 406 or 407

matches.name: St. Columba of Sens
matches.ceNote: Woman martyred towards the end of the third century

matches.name: St. Columbanus
matches.ceNote: Irish-born abbot of Luxeuil and Bobbio, author of a monastic rule and of a penitential, d. 615. Biography

matches.name: St. Constantine the Great
matches.ceNote: Information on the Roman emperor

matches.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
matches.ceNote: Bishop, Doctor of the Church, d. 386

matches.name: St. Damasus I
matches.ceNote: Damasus, who had to contend with an antipope, condemned Apollinarianism, and persuaded St. Jerome to undertake the revision of the Latin Bible, died in 384

matches.name: St. Didymus the Blind
matches.ceNote: Layman, one of the principal opponents of Arianism. Born about 310-313; died about 395-398

matches.name: St. Dionysius of Alexandria
matches.ceNote: Also called Dionysius the Great. Bishop, d. 264 or 265

matches.name: St. Donatus of Fiesole
matches.ceNote: Irish teacher and poet, Bishop of Fiesole, about 829-876

matches.name: St. Edward the Confessor
matches.ceNote: Short biography of the King of England, who died in 1066

matches.name: St. Edward the Martyr
matches.ceNote: King of England, assassinated at the age of 16 or 17 at the behest of his stepmother. St. Edward was murdered in 979

matches.name: St. Eimhin
matches.ceNote: Abbot and Bishop of Ros-mic-Truin, d. first half of the sixth century. Some believe that Eimhin is the author of the Tripartite Life of St. Patrick

matches.name: St. Elias I of Jerusalem
matches.ceNote: Died 518; one of the two Catholic bishops (with Flavian of Antioch) who resisted the attempt of the Emperor Anastasius I (491-518) to abolish the Council of Chalcedon (451)

matches.name: St. Emerentiana
matches.ceNote: Virgin and martyr, d. at Rome in the third century

matches.name: St. Eucharius
matches.ceNote: First bishop of Trier (Treves). Second half of third century

matches.name: St. Eugenius of Carthage
matches.ceNote: Unanimously elected bishop of Carthage, exiled for a time for speaking out against the Arians, died 505

matches.name: St. Florentina
matches.ceNote: Sometimes called Florentia. Spanish nun, d. about 612

matches.name: St. Fructuosus of Braga
matches.ceNote: Hermit, abbot, archbishop, d. around 665

matches.name: St. Gaudentius of Brescia
matches.ceNote: A theologian of the Order of Friars Minor Capuchins; b. at Brescia in 1612; d. at Oriano, 25 March, 1672

matches.name: St. Gilbert of Sempringham
matches.ceNote: Short biography of the founder of the Gilbertines, who died in 1189

matches.name: St. Gildas
matches.ceNote: Biographical entry for St. Gildas the Wise, also called 'Badonicus,' born to a British family in Scotland, educated in Wales, monk, priest, died in 570

matches.name: St. Gregory I
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this Doctor of the Church, d. 604

matches.name: St. Gregory II
matches.ceNote: Also known as Gregory Junior, or Gregory the Younger, d. 731

matches.name: St. Gregory III
matches.ceNote: A Syrian, was elected the successor of Pope St. Gregory II by acclamation, d. 741

matches.name: St. Gregory of Nazianzus
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this Doctor of the Church, known in the Christian East as St. Gregory the Theologian

matches.name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
matches.ceNote: Bishop, one of the Cappadocian Fathers, d. after 385 or 386

matches.name: St. Hegesippus
matches.ceNote: Second-century writer, opposed Marcionism and Gnosticism

matches.name: St. Hesychius of Sinai
matches.ceNote: A priest and monk of the Order of St. Basil in the Thorn-bush (Batos) monastery on Mt. Sinai, and ascetic author of the Byzantine period in literature

matches.name: St. Hilary of Arles
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this 5th-century archbishop

matches.name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this bishop, a staunch opponent of Arianism, who died in 368. Includes bibliography

matches.name: St. Honoratus
matches.ceNote: Founder of the famous monastery at Lerins, Archbishop of Arles, d. 429

matches.name: St. Irenaeus
matches.ceNote: Article on the bishop of Lyons, Father of the Church, d. late second or early third century

matches.name: St. Isaac of Armenia
matches.ceNote: Catholicos or Patriarch of Armenia (338-439)

matches.name: St. Isidore of Pelusium
matches.ceNote: Born at Alexandria, became a monk, opposed Nestorianism and Eutychianism, d. no later than 449-450

matches.name: St. John Cassian
matches.ceNote: Article on the monk and ascetic writer, who attempted to convey the teaching and way of life of the desert fathers and mothers to the fledgling monastic movement in Gaul

matches.name: St. John Climacus
matches.ceNote: Sometimes called Scholasticus or the Sinaita. Article on the sixth-century Syrian abbot of Mt. Sinai. He is called 'Climacus' because he wrote the spiritual classic 'The Ladder of Divine Ascent,' 'Klimax' being the Greek for 'ladder.'

matches.name: St. John of Beverley
matches.ceNote: Benedictine bishop of Hexham and later of York, monastic founder, d. 721

matches.name: St. John the Silent
matches.ceNote: Or John Hesychastes. Monk, runaway bishop of Colonia, hermit, d. 558

matches.name: St. Jonas of Bobbio
matches.ceNote: Monk and hagiographer, b. about the close of the sixth century at Sigusia (Susa) in Piedmont; d. after 659

matches.name: St. Julius I
matches.ceNote: A Roman, anti-Arian, supporter of St. Athanasius. Julius died in 352

matches.name: St. Leo II
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this pontiff, who died in 683

matches.name: St. Leo IV
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this Roman, who died in 855

matches.name: St. Leo IX
matches.ceNote: Hagiographical article on this reformer pope, who died in 1054

matches.name: St. Macrina the Elder
matches.ceNote: Grandmother of SS. Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa, and Macrina the Younger

matches.name: St. Magnus Felix Ennodius
matches.ceNote: Rhetorician and bishop, b. probably at Arles, in Southern Gaul, in 474; d. at Pavia, Italy, 17 July, 521

matches.name: St. Manahen
matches.ceNote: Or Manaen. Mentioned in Scripture, and traditionally believed to have been one of the first Christians in Antioch

matches.name: St. Marcellina
matches.ceNote: Consecrated virgin, blood sister of St. Ambrose, d. about 398

matches.name: St. Marcellus I
matches.ceNote: After a vacancy in office following the death of Pope St. Marcellinus, was elected to the papacy in 308. Fairly lengthy biographical article

matches.name: St. Martial
matches.ceNote: Third-century bishop of Limoges

matches.name: St. Maximus of Turin
matches.ceNote: Bishop and theological writer (380-465)

matches.name: St. Meletius of Antioch
matches.ceNote: Lengthy article on the career of the gentle bishop who longed for unity in the Church

matches.name: St. Mellitus
matches.ceNote: Archbishop of Canterbury, died in 624. Abbot sent to Canterbury by St. Gregory the Great, and the recipient of a letter from Gregory regarding pagan temples, idols, and festivals

matches.name: St. Nicholas I
matches.ceNote: Biography of this pope, d. 867, who upheld the authority of the papacy and the inviolability of marriage

matches.name: St. Nilus the Younger
matches.ceNote: Calabrian monk, hermit, founder, d. 1005

matches.name: St. Olaf Haraldsson
matches.ceNote: Martyr and King of Norway, d. 1030

matches.name: St. Optatus
matches.ceNote: Fairly long essay on the life and writings of this bishop, who argued against the Donatists. He died in about 387

matches.name: St. Osmund
matches.ceNote: A Norman by birth, Osmund became bishop of Salisbury, and died in 1099

matches.name: St. Pammachius
matches.ceNote: Roman senator, widower, friend of SS. Augustine and Jerome, d. 409

matches.name: St. Pantaenus
matches.ceNote: Head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria about 180, still alive in 193

matches.name: St. Paschal I
matches.ceNote: Pope who reigned from 817 to 824

matches.name: St. Perpetuus
matches.ceNote: Eighth bishop of Tours, d. 490 or 491. St. Perpetuus was greatly devoted to his predecessor St. Martin of Tours

matches.name: St. Peter Chrysologus
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Ravenna, d. 450. Pious, zealous, and a renowned speaker--thus the name 'Chrysologus'

matches.name: St. Philastrius
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Brescia, died before 397. Catalogued heresies, and preached especially against Arianism

matches.name: St. Plegmund
matches.ceNote: Archbishop of Canterbury (d. 914)

matches.name: St. Porphyrius
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Gaza, died in 420

matches.name: St. Possidius
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Calama, was a friend of St. Augustine for 40 years

matches.name: St. Pulcheria
matches.ceNote: Empress of the Eastern Roman Empire, staunch opponent of Nestorianism and Eutychianism, d. 453

matches.name: St. Rimbert
matches.ceNote: Monk and archbishop of Bremen-Hamburg (d. 888)

matches.name: St. Sabina
matches.ceNote: Martyr in 126 or 127, at Rome

matches.name: St. Stephen I
matches.ceNote: Reigned 254-257

matches.name: St. Trudpert
matches.ceNote: Seventh-century missionary in Germany

matches.name: St. Ultan of Ardbraccan
matches.ceNote: Collected a life of the Irish saint for his pupil, St. Brogan Cloen of Rostuirc, on Ossory

matches.name: St. Wilfrid
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on this abbot and bishop, who died in 709

matches.name: St. Willehad
matches.ceNote: Short biography of the missionary and bishop, d. 789

matches.name: St. William of Gellone
matches.ceNote: Late eighth century. The second count of Toulouse, founded a Benedictine monastery, then became a monk himself

matches.name: St. Winnoc
matches.ceNote: Early eighth-century Benedictine prior

matches.name: St. Zachary
matches.ceNote: Biography of this eighth-century pontiff, with special emphasis on his diplomacy and his relations with St. Boniface

matches.name: St. Zephyrinus
matches.ceNote: Fairly long article on this pontiff, who died in 217

matches.name: Pope Hormisdas
matches.ceNote: Died 523. The father of Pope Silverius

matches.name: Pope Pontian
matches.ceNote: He was exiled to the Sardinian mines in 235 and died there of privation

matches.name: Pope Siricius
matches.ceNote: Siricius condemned Jovinian, but this did not spare the pope from criticism by St. Jerome

matches.name: St. Abdias of Babylon
matches.ceNote: Apocryphal writer

matches.name: St. Adeodatus I
matches.ceNote: Also known as Pope Adeodatus I, d. 618

matches.name: St. Agapetus I
matches.ceNote: Anti-Arian, instrumental in deposing a Monophysite bishop who had moreover abandoned his see, d. 536

matches.name: St. Agatho
matches.ceNote: Short article on St. Agatho the Wonderworker, a Sicilian believed to have been over 100 years old at the time of his election. He died in 681

matches.name: St. Alphonsus Liguori
matches.ceNote: Long biographical article on the founder of the Redemptorists and devotional writer

matches.name: St. Anacletus
matches.ceNote: Third pope, a martyr, d. about 91. May be the same person as Pope St. Cletus

matches.name: St. Anastasius I
matches.ceNote: Article on the pope remembered chiefly for condemning Origenism, d. 401

matches.name: St. Anicetus
matches.ceNote: Biography of this martyr, a contemporary of St. Polycarp and of the heretic Marcion

matches.name: St. Anterus
matches.ceNote: Also known as Anteros, pope for less than 2 months, d. in 236. Short biographical article

matches.name: St. Apollinaris Claudius
matches.ceNote: Second-century bishop of Hierapolis, apologist

matches.name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on the monk who was the first Archbishop of Canterbury, called 'Apostle of the English.'

matches.name: St. Ava
matches.ceNote: A German poetess, the first woman known to have written in German and probably identical with a recluse of that name who died in Austria in the vicinity of Melk, A.D. 1127

matches.name: St. Benedict Biscop
matches.ceNote: Anglo-Saxon, monastic founder, d. 690

matches.name: St. Benedict II
matches.ceNote: A Roman, he was pope for a little less than eleven months, and died in 685. Account of his pontificate

matches.name: St. Berach
matches.ceNote: A disciple of St. Kevin. Abbot of Cluain Coirpthe, now called Kilbarry or Termonbarry in the saint's honor. St. Berach died in 595

matches.name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
matches.ceNote: Article on the life and works of this twelfth-century Cistercian and Doctor of the Church

matches.name: St. Beuno
matches.ceNote: Welsh, said to have been educated at Bangor and, after ordination, to have become a missionary. Abbot of Clynnog, and uncle of St. Winifred. Died perhaps in 660

matches.name: St. Boisil
matches.ceNote: Abbot of Melrose, renowned for prophetic gifts, taught St. Cuthbert. St. Boisil died in 664

matches.name: St. Boniface I
matches.ceNote: Consecrated the same day as the antipope Eulalius. Both were ordered to leave Rome. Eulalius took over St. John Lateran on Holy Saturday, after which the emperor refused to consider his claim. Boniface died in 422

matches.name: St. Boniface IV
matches.ceNote: Transformed the Pantheon into a Christian church, died in 615

matches.name: St. Bridget of Sweden
matches.ceNote: Biography of the mother of 8, widow, visionary, founder of the Brigittines

matches.name: St. Bruno of Querfurt
matches.ceNote: Courtier, monk, missionary archbishop, hagiographer, martyr. Called the Second Apostle of the Prussians

matches.name: St. Caesarius of Nazianzus
matches.ceNote: Physician, brother of St. Gregory of Nazianzus (the Theologian). Caesarius died in late 368 or early 369

matches.name: St. Cedd
matches.ceNote: Brother of St. Chad (Ceadda) and bishop of the East Saxons, d. 664

matches.name: St. Chrysogonus
matches.ceNote: Martyr at Aquileia, probably during the Diocletian persecution

matches.name: St. Colman
matches.ceNote: Irishman martyred while on pilgrimage to Jerusalem, near Vienna in 1012

matches.name: St. Columba of Terryglass
matches.ceNote: A disciple of St. Finnian of Clonard, and himself taught St. Fintan. This St. Columba founded the monastery of Tirdaglas, and died of the plague in 552

matches.name: St. Conan
matches.ceNote: Also known as Mochonna. Irish missionary and Bishop of the Isle of Man, d. 684

matches.name: St. Crescens
matches.ceNote: A companion of St. Paul during his second Roman captivity, appears but once in the New Testament, when he is mentioned as having left the Apostle to go into Galatia

matches.name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
matches.ceNote: Article on this Doctor of the Church, and anti-Nestorian theologian

matches.name: St. Díchu
matches.ceNote: The son of an Ulster chieftain, was the first convert of St. Patrick in Ireland

matches.name: St. Drostan
matches.ceNote: Scottish abbot and later hermit, fl. about 600. Also known as St. Drustan, Dustan, or Throstan

matches.name: St. Earconwald
matches.ceNote: Monk, Bishop of London, founded two monasteries, d. about 690. Biography

matches.name: St. Edmund Campion
matches.ceNote: English Jesuit, martyr, d. 1581. Biographical article

matches.name: St. Ephraim of Antioch
matches.ceNote: One of the defenders of the Faith of Chalcedon (451) against the Monophysites, b. at Amida in Mesopotamia; d. in 545

matches.name: St. Eugendus
matches.ceNote: Fourth abbot of Condat, d. 510. Also called St. Augendus, Oyand, or Oyan

matches.name: St. Evodius
matches.ceNote: The first Bishop of Antioch after St. Peter

matches.name: St. Exuperius
matches.ceNote: Or Exsuperius. Early fifth-century bishop of Toulouse

matches.name: St. Faustus of Riez
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Riez in Southern Gaul, the best known and most distinguished defender of Semipelagianism, b. between 405 and 410, d. between 490 and 495

matches.name: St. Fiacc
matches.ceNote: Poet, chief bishop of Leinster, d. around 520

matches.name: St. Finnian of Movilla
matches.ceNote: Irish monk, author of a monastic rule and a penitential. Also the founder of a famous school in County Down. St. Finnian died in 589

matches.name: St. Firmilian
matches.ceNote: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, died c. 269

matches.name: St. Flavia Domitilla
matches.ceNote: A Christian Roman matron of the imperial family who lived towards the close of the first century

matches.name: St. Francis Xavier
matches.ceNote: Biographical article on one of the first Jesuits, and missionary to Asia, who died in 1552

matches.name: St. Gabriel the Archangel
matches.ceNote: One of the three archangels mentioned in the Bible

matches.name: St. Gertrude the Great
matches.ceNote: Benedictine, mystic, author, d. 1301 or 1302

matches.name: St. Ghislain
matches.ceNote: Hermit in Belgium, confessor, died c. 680

matches.name: St. Gregory the Illuminator
matches.ceNote: Patron of Armenia. Husband and father, bishop, d. possibly in 337

matches.name: St. Gregory VII
matches.ceNote: Also known as Hildebrand: 'one of the greatest of the Roman pontiffs and one of the most remarkable men of all times.' He died in 1085. Biographical article

matches.name: St. Helena
matches.ceNote: The mother of Constantine the Great, she died about 330

matches.name: St. Herbert of Derwentwater
matches.ceNote: Short biography of the seventh-century anchorite

matches.name: St. Hereswith
matches.ceNote: Also known as Haeresvid or Hereswyde, blood sister of St. Hilda of Whitby. Mother, widow, and nun

matches.name: St. Hermenegild
matches.ceNote: The son of an Arian Visigothic king. His mother and wife were Catholic, and he converted to Catholicism, and resisted Arianism. He was beheaded in 585

matches.name: St. Hilarion
matches.ceNote: Hermit, died in about 371

matches.name: St. Hilarius
matches.ceNote: As an archdeacon, he had acted as one of Pope St. Leo the Great's legates at the 'Robber Synod.' Biographical article

matches.name: St. Hugh of Lincoln
matches.ceNote: Biography of this Augustinian and later a Carthusian, d. 1200, canonized 1220

matches.name: St. Hyginus
matches.ceNote: Greek by birth, the successor of Pope Telesphorus. Died in about 142

matches.name: St. Ignatios of Constantinople
matches.ceNote: Tells the story of this son of Emperor Michael I, forced into monastic life by a rival. Patriarch of Constantinople, deposed on a wicked pretext. Ignatius died in 877

matches.name: St. Innocent I
matches.ceNote: Unanimously chosen to succeed Anastasius. Essay on his writings and some of the more notable events of his pontificate. Innocent died in 417

matches.name: St. Jacob Baradaeus
matches.ceNote: A Syrian Monophysite bishop, born in Tella, towards the end of the fifth or the beginning of the sixth century, died in 578

matches.name: St. Jane Frances de Chantal

matches.name: St. John of Avila

matches.name: St. Paul
